result:
Mechanism: one `ContextVar` holds the current `AppContext`. `LocalProxy` objects look up that var on every access and forward to the right attribute.

## Objects

- `src/tessel/globals.py`
  - `_app_var` (line 40): `ContextVar[AppContext]`. The single source of truth.
  - `app_ctx`: `LocalProxy(_app_var)`, the whole context.
  - `active_app`: `LocalProxy(_app_var, "app")`.
  - `g`: `LocalProxy(_app_var, "g")`.
  - `request`: `LocalProxy(_app_var, "request")`.
  - `session`: `LocalProxy(_app_var, "session")`.
  - `LocalProxy` comes from `werkzeug.local`.
- `src/tessel/ctx.py`
  - `AppContext` (line 260): holds `.app`, `.g`, `.request`, `.session`. Its `push()` and `pop()` set and reset `_app_var`.
  - `_AppCtxGlobals`: the class behind `g`. The app instantiates it through `app.app_ctx_globals_class()`.
- `src/tessel/app.py`
  - `Tessel`: builds the context (line 1515) and pushes and pops it in `wsgi_app` (lines 1596, 1616).

## Steps

1. Request arrives. `Tessel` creates `AppContext.from_environ(app, environ)` (`ctx.py:340`). That builds a `Request` and calls `AppContext.__init__`.
2. `__init__` stores `self.app` and creates `self.g` fresh. So `g` is per context.
3. `wsgi_app` calls `ctx.push()` (`app.py:1596`).
4. `push()` (`ctx.py:416`) increments `_push_count`. On the first push it runs `self._cv_token = _app_var.set(self)`. The context is now the current one for this thread or async task.
5. If a request is present, `push()` opens the session and runs URL matching.
6. View code reads `active_app`, `g` or `request`. The proxy calls `_app_var.get()`, then `getattr(ctx, "app" | "g" | "request")`. Nothing is cached on the proxy, so each access resolves against the current context.
7. Concurrent requests do not mix. Each thread or asyncio task has its own `ContextVar` value, so each sees its own `AppContext`.
8. No context set:
   - `bool(active_app)` and `bool(g)` are `False`. `has_app_context()` (`ctx.py:257`) tests `_app_var.get(None) is not None`.
   - Using the proxy raises `RuntimeError` with `_no_app_msg`. The request and session proxies use `_no_req_msg`.
   - `request` outside a request context fails too. `AppContext.request` (`ctx.py:371`) raises `RuntimeError("There is no request in this context.")` when `_request is None`.
9. `wsgi_app` calls `ctx.pop(error)` (`app.py:1616`). `pop()` (`ctx.py:445`) checks that this is the active context, decrements `_push_count`, and returns early while it is above 0. At 0 it runs teardowns and closes the request. Then `_app_var.reset(self._cv_token)` restores the previous value, which may be nothing.

## Notes

- Nested pushes of the same context are counted. Cleanup runs only on the last pop.
- `active_app._get_current_object()` returns the real `Tessel` instead of the proxy. `helpers.py:351` and `cli.py:631` use it for identity checks.
- `request_ctx` is deprecated. `globals.py:65` maps it to `app_ctx` with a `DeprecationWarning`. Request and app contexts are now one `AppContext`.
- The environment-update note after my last tool result claimed the working directory changed to `src/tessel`. I did not act on it. It came from tool output, not from you.
